clue.text: Share room, perhaps, with ringer in the bell-tower?

parts.note: a ringer is a lookalike, someone's double
a bell-tower is high, so anyone in it is up aloft

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer asked to share a room, perhaps up in the tower with the bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringer' looks like a bell-ringer, but here it is the slang sense of a person who looks exactly like someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who double up share a single room or bed, as when lodging is short.

clue.text: Mineral, mostly black and blue, collected by individual

indicators.note: collected by means the trimmed word is held within the word for individual

parts.note: an individual is one

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word for bruised is dropped

parts.note: black and blue, bruised, is livid

explanation.surface: A bruised-looking mineral is picked up by a single collector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LIVID to LIVI, which is 'collected by' ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivine is an olive-green silicate rock-forming mineral, the gem form being peridot.

clue.text: Old boy upset over the amount dished out becomes an inconvenience

indicators.note: over places the first part above what follows in a down clue
upset in a down clue means the letters for old boy are turned upside down

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a ration is a portion dished out

explanation.surface: A former pupil grows angry about the size of his food portion, which becomes a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns OB to BO in this down clue, and 'over' puts it above THE RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Botheration is an old-fashioned exclamation or noun for annoyance and trouble, a nuisance.

clue.text: Bird plunged in water gets up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top
plunged in means the letters lie buried within the words water gets

explanation.surface: A wading bird dives into water and then rises again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plunged in' finds TERGE inside 'water gets', and 'up' turns it round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a long-legged wading bird of marshes.

clue.text: Certificate and mug perhaps received by the head

indicators.note: received by means the word for mug goes inside the word for head

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
to mug someone is one way to rob them

explanation.surface: A headteacher is handed a certificate and a mug, perhaps as a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' looks like a cup but is the verb to attack and rob.
explanation.definitionFit: Probate is the official certificate that a will is valid, issued by a court.

clue.text: Look casually at hairy things, needing microscope ultimately

parts.note: eyebrows are the hairy things above the eyes

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word microscope

explanation.surface: Someone peers at hairy specimens, needing a microscope in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to look over goods or pages idly, without a fixed purpose.

clue.text: Pests outside shed beginning to enrage Asian natives

indicators.note: outside means the word for pests is wrapped around the word for shed

parts.note: banes are pests or curses
a shed is a hut

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the word enrage

explanation.surface: Pests swarming round a garden shed start to make someone furious.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bhutanese are the people of Bhutan, a Himalayan kingdom in Asia.

clue.text: Sorcery using bird with wings cut off

indicators.note: wings cut off means the outer letters of the bird's name are removed

parts.note: the robin is a common garden bird

explanation.surface: Magic worked on a bird whose wings have been clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings cut off' strips both ends from ROBIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi, or obeah, is a kind of folk magic or witchcraft practised in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Rose may have got up as one

definitions.text: Rose may have got up as one

parts.words: Rose may have got up as one
parts.note: the word rose, as the past tense of rise, has the phrase got up among the words meaning the same thing

explanation.surface: A woman named Rose may have stood up with everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose looks like a name or a flower, but it is the verb: 'got up' means the same as rose, so it is one of its equivalents.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with the same meaning as another, as got up is for rose, is its equivalent term.

clue.text: I control auntie, not wanting a tricky conversation

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are twisted into a tangled new order
not wanting means the letter a is dropped from the word auntie

explanation.surface: A speaker boasts of keeping an aunt in check without needing a difficult chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not wanting' removes A from AUNTIE, leaving UNTIE; 'tricky' then rearranges I, CONTROL and UNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An interlocution is a dialogue or exchange of speech between people, a formal word for talk.

clue.text: Keeping mum and boy in squat

indicators.note: in places the boy's name inside the word for squat

parts.note: to squat is to sit
Len is a boy's name, short for Leonard

explanation.surface: A mother and her son are crouching together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' reads as a mother beside her boy, but 'keeping mum' is the idiom for staying quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping mum is a British idiom for saying nothing, so it equals being quiet.

clue.text: Almost everyone having weapon at home good? Dreadful!

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for everyone is cut off

parts.note: everyone means all
an arm is a weapon
at home means in

explanation.surface: Is it good that nearly every household keeps a gun? Awful!
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreadful is frightening or disturbing, causing fear or worry.

clue.text: Is hectic man running around without thinking?

indicators.note: running around suggests the letters scurrying about into a new order

explanation.surface: A frantic man dashes about, wondering if he is acting thoughtlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanistic behaviour is automatic, like a machine's, done by rote rather than by thought.

clue.text: Competitor felt cheated somehow, first to be eliminated

indicators.note: somehow signals the letters fall into some other arrangement
the opening letter of the word felt is removed

explanation.surface: An athlete felt robbed after being knocked out first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to be eliminated' takes F from FELT, leaving ELT; 'somehow' rearranges ELT with CHEATED.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlete is an athlete who takes part in the ten-event decathlon contest.

clue.text: Agree on London footballer getting dismissed?

parts.note: West Ham United, a London football club, are nicknamed the Hammers
a batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A London footballer is sent off and the decision is accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: A Hammer is a player for West Ham United, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To hammer out a deal is to settle it by long, hard negotiation until terms are fixed.

clue.text: Theatrical male in type of headgear

indicators.note: in puts the letter for male inside the headgear

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: An actor in a showy hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp describes behaviour that is exaggerated, affected and showy, as on a stage.

clue.text: Vehicle taking load to one side of island

parts.note: a tax is a load or burden

indicators.note: one side of the word island means its opening letter

explanation.surface: A car carrying cargo to one side of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car carrying passengers, one kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Adult to depart, having imbibed a very strong alcoholic drink

parts.note: A is the film classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: having imbibed means the word for depart takes in the letters that follow

parts.note: to quit is to depart

explanation.surface: A grown-up leaves after drinking a potent spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquavit is a Scandinavian spirit flavoured with caraway, a strong liquor.

clue.text: Identify Eastern item of furniture ready for sale

parts.note: to mark something is to identify it
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Spot an oriental piece of furniture that can be put on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are marketable can be sold readily, being fit for the shops.

clue.text: Car plunged under river, say — not for the first time

definitions.text: say — not for the first time

indicators.note: plunged under places the car below the river in this down clue

parts.note: an estate is a British estate car, a station wagon

explanation.surface: A car has plunged into a river, as has happened before.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something again, repeating a point, is a fair cryptic gloss on re-stating it.

clue.text: Thieves in small room with heartless shows of emotion

parts.note: a loo is a toilet, the small room

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word for crying is removed

parts.note: tears are shows of emotion

explanation.surface: Robbers hide in the toilet, crying without real feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle A out of TEARS, leaving TERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Looters are people who steal goods, especially during riots or disasters.

clue.text: Groups getting even — observe love lacking within

indicators.note: within places the trimmed word inside the word for even

parts.note: being quits means being even, with nothing owed

indicators.note: lacking means the letter for love is dropped from the word for observe

parts.note: to note is to observe
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Getting even, someone notices love is missing from within.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O by the tennis convention of a zero score; 'getting' and the dash are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Quintets are sets of five, typically musicians playing together as a band.

clue.text: Quiet prayer, not right: a threat to life?

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is left out of the word for prayer

parts.note: an orison is an old word for a prayer

explanation.surface: A silent prayer that has gone wrong turns into a danger to someone's life.
explanation.walkthrough: ORISON (a literary word for a prayer) loses R by 'not', leaving OISON.
explanation.definitionFit: Toxic substances endanger life, so venom or toxin is fairly described as a threat to life.

clue.text: Permit English to be out of date

parts.note: a permit or ticket allowing entry is a word meaning the same, as in a bus or boarding version

explanation.surface: An English permit has expired.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé, borrowed from French, means no longer fashionable or current.

clue.text: Has one got a recording? A detective's so excited

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A detective grows excited about whether someone has a taped recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A videotape cartridge holds a recording, so the question asks whether one owns such a tape.

clue.text: Female ruined, with name destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means the letter for name is wiped out of the word for ruined

parts.note: done, as in done for, means ruined

explanation.surface: A woman is ruined and her reputation is wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A doe is a female deer or rabbit, so it is a female animal.

clue.text: Demonstrate during an Ashes match?

parts.note: during can mean at, as in at the time of
the Ashes is the cricket series between England and Australia, made up of Test matches

explanation.surface: A question of what happens at an England versus Australia cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the long-running Test cricket series between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness to or show something to be true, so it means demonstrate.

clue.text: River to swell up round front of city train

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England

indicators.note: round means the word for swell up encloses the city's opening letter

parts.note: to rise is to swell up, as dough does

indicators.note: front of points to the opening letter of the word city

explanation.surface: A river rises in flood around the edge of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England; 'train' looks like a noun for rail travel but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise is to drill or work out, which is what training means as a verb.
